classification.difficultyReason: Establish a right angle from bearings, then use an inverse trigonometric ratio to determine a new bearing.

content.prompt: A ship leaves port $P$ and travels 150 nautical miles to port $Q$ on a bearing of $110^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$. It then travels 120 nautical miles to port $R$ on a bearing of $200^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle PQR with parallel dashed north arrows at P and Q, clockwise 110-degree bearing arc at P and clockwise reflex 200-degree bearing arc at Q. No side lengths or right-angle mark are printed.
spec.mathematics: P=(0,0); Q=5(sin110°,cos110°); R=Q+4(sin200°,cos200°). The leg ratio is 150:120. Bearing arcs run from TikZ angle 90° to −20° at P and −110° at Q.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied geometry, point labels and bearing labels are visible; answers and derived angles are omitted.

answer.short: $\angle PQR=360^{\circ}-(200^{\circ}+70^{\circ})=90^{\circ}$, using co-interior angles on parallel north lines and angles about a point.
answer.worked:
The north lines are parallel, so the angle between $QP$ and north at $Q$ is $180^{\circ}-110^{\circ}=70^{\circ}$ by co-interior angles. Angles about $Q$ sum to $360^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle PQR&=360^{\circ}-(200^{\circ}+70^{\circ})\\&=90^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the bearing of $R$ from $P$ to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
Let $\theta=\angle QPR$. In the right-angled triangle, $QR$ is opposite $\theta$ and $PQ$ is adjacent.
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{120}{150}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{120}{150}\right).\end{align*}$$
The bearing of $PR$ is clockwise beyond the bearing of $PQ$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of }R\text{ from }P&=110^{\circ}+\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{120}{150}\right)\\&\approx149^{\circ}\mathrm{T}.\end{align*}$$
